commentary:
Risk appetite is firming into the weekend, with the story led by a weaker dollar and a roaring precious-metals bid. The US Treasury's plan to buy back longer-dated bonds has stabilised yields, knocked the greenback lower across the board, and sent hard assets flying: gold +1.8% at 4,654, silver +2.7%, platinum +3%, and copper +2.2% as the softer dollar and firm risk tone pull the industrial complex along. Bitcoin is on track for its best week in over three years, equity-index futures are higher with the Nasdaq 100 (+0.8%) set to snap a five-day slide, and AI-sector optimism got a fresh boost from Samsung's plan to return up to $80bn to shareholders.

The macro tension underneath is unresolved: buybacks cap the long end tactically, but structurally higher term premium — governments and AI hyperscalers competing for capital amid sticky inflation risk — argues against chasing duration, and Treasuries trimmed early gains. Fed Chair Warsh at Jackson Hole next week is the asymmetric risk for rates futures, according to reports; meanwhile traders are bracing for a more hawkish ECB and UK August PMIs beat handily, supporting sterling and capping Gilt upside. Crude is the outlier — Brent -0.4% near $93 — though Dec-Dec spreads at their strongest since mid-May signal a tight physical market, with Washington's plan to squeeze Iran's economy a lingering supply risk.

Henry Hub and TTF gas are both up ~1.6% on German storage shortfalls. Ags are soft across wheat and the tropicals; hogs fell 1.6% on ground-beef tariff relief. Watch Jackson Hole and Nvidia's results as the next catalysts.
